channel.title: AI Tool Reviews (#fragRoger)
channel.description: Every Sunday, six AI tools assessed for value, cost and data protection.

item.title: Week 42/2026: Talanoa, Canvora, Caldera, Articos v3.2, WEXTL, noScribe, Sally
item.description:
This week the value of AI shifts from the single output to the controllable work context. Talanoa and Caldera show how local data storage and selective publishing enable productivity without an additional content cloud. Canvora, Articos and WEXTL bring design, research and automation into existing processes, but require a clear review of data flows, costs and approvals. A new tool only becomes useful once permissions, exceptions and the exit path are as clear as the demo.

  • Text: Talanoa (8.2/10). Local email client with AI for search, summaries and reply drafts.
  • Design: Canvora (7.8/10). On-brand visuals and slides from text, URLs and documents, with MCP integration.
  • Data / Knowledge: Caldera (7.9/10). Open-source Obsidian plugin for a local vault, selective publishing and digital gardens.
  • Research: Articos v3.2 (7.4/10). Synthetic user research with an MCP server, credit-based billing and an audience-first workflow.
  • Agents: WEXTL (7.7/10). Visual builder for AI agents and approval-driven workflow automation.
  • Transcription: noScribe (8.3/10). Free open-source desktop app that transcribes interviews and other sensitive recordings entirely on your own computer.
  • Transcription: Sally (8.4/10). AI meeting assistant from Mannheim that transcribes, summarises and translates online, hybrid and in-person meetings in more than 100 languages.

item.title: Week 40/2026: Claude Sonnet 5.5, Suno Speech Beta, Strands Decider 2B, Slashspace 3.3, Dots by OpenAI
item.description:
This week AI becomes valuable where an answer turns into controllable execution. Claude Sonnet 5.5 speeds up clearly bounded knowledge work, while Strands Decider 2B carries out small routine decisions locally and with a confidence score. Suno Speech lowers the barrier for audio prototypes, Slashspace connects research in a local canvas and Dots shows the potential of persistent cloud agents. Data flows, permissions, regional availability and human approval remain decisive.

  • Text: Claude Sonnet 5.5 (8.8/10). Faster model for clearly bounded knowledge and implementation work.
  • Design: Suno Speech Beta (7.4/10). Spoken audio with an original music bed as one continuous track.
  • Data / Knowledge: Strands Decider 2B (8.2/10). Open-source decision model for local triage, routing and guardrails.
  • Research: Slashspace 3.3 (7.8/10). Local-first canvas for multi-model research, sources and orchestration.
  • Agents: Dots by OpenAI (7/10). Persistent cloud agents with app connections, rules and an activity view.

item.title: Week 38/2026: Claude Docs, Arrow 2, Jev, Sakana Marlin, Octop
item.description:
This week AI becomes valuable where an answer turns into an editable and verifiable work result. Claude Docs makes documents the context of a conversation, Arrow 2 delivers editable SVGs and Jev translates uncertainty into structured software decisions. Sakana Marlin leads from research results back to the sources, while Octop brings agents onto your own infrastructure. Data residency, approval rights, cost limits and the ability not only to generate results but also to check them remain decisive.

  • Text: Claude Docs (8.5/10). Document mode in the Claude workspace with direct editing and export.
  • Design: Arrow 2 (8/10). Editable SVG generation, vectorisation and animation with a production-grade API.
  • Data / Knowledge: Jev (8/10). Typed decisions with confidence scores for software automation.
  • Research: Sakana Marlin (8/10). Deep research agent with evidence checks and editable PowerPoint export.
  • Agents: Octop (8.2/10). MIT-licensed, self-hosted multi-agent platform for controlled workflows.

item.title: Week 37/2026: Typewise Nova, Suno v6, AI Toolbox 3.0, Scira, OpenAI Agents API
item.description:
This week the value of AI shifts from the single output to the controllable work system. Typewise Nova operates customer service, AI Toolbox 3.0 organises scattered chat knowledge, Scira makes research sources more visible and the OpenAI Agents API puts managed agent infrastructure within reach. Suno v6 delivers more creative control but also shows clearly that generating is not the same as ready to publish. Rights, data flow, cost limits and human approvals remain decisive.

  • Text: Typewise Nova (8/10). AI operator for customer service with controlled end-to-end handling.
  • Design: Suno v6 (8/10). Generative music with more targeted edit, mashup and multimodal workflows.
  • Data / Knowledge: AI Toolbox 3.0 (8/10). Full-text search, folders and export for ChatGPT, Gemini, Claude and Grok.
  • Research: Scira (8/10). Source-based research with many search modes and open code.
  • Agents: OpenAI Agents API (8/10). Managed agent infrastructure for long-running sessions, tools and sub-agents.

item.title: Week 36/2026: Claude Fable 5.1, Atlas von World Labs, HubSpot AEO + AI Search Sensor, Articos, Ritto AI
item.description:
This week AI improves where it makes the work context more controllable. Claude Fable 5.1 combines text work with a relevant retention architecture; Atlas turns space and camera into controllable design parameters. HubSpot AEO, Articos and Ritto show three different paths: measurability, hypothesis testing and demonstrated automation. The productive question is not "What can the AI do?" but "What can I clearly limit, check and take responsibility for?"

  • Text: Claude Fable 5.1 (8.7/10). Demanding text and knowledge work with cheaper reusable context.
  • Design: Atlas von World Labs (7.8/10). Spatially controlled image, video and 3D generation for creative concept work.
  • Data / Knowledge: HubSpot AEO + AI Search Sensor (8.2/10). Measurable visibility in AI answers with source, prompt and industry context.
  • Research: Articos (7.5/10). Synthetic user research for quick hypotheses on messaging, UX and offering.
  • Agents: Ritto AI (6.8/10). Demonstrate recurring screen work once, repeat it in a controlled batch.

item.title: Week 35/2026: Claude mit Memory, Midjourney V8.2 Edit Model, PageIndex SDK Local, Lenz, Construct Computer
item.description:
This week the value of AI shifts from the single answer to the controllable work context. Claude makes memory editable, Midjourney makes image changes more targeted, PageIndex makes document knowledge executable locally, Lenz makes claims verifiable and Construct makes multi-step work persistent. The productive question is not "What can the AI do?" but "What can I trace, limit and reuse?"

  • Text: Claude mit Memory (8.5/10). Editable work context across chat and Cowork.
  • Design: Midjourney V8.2 Edit Model (8.5/10). Targeted image editing with instructions and up to four references.
  • Data / Knowledge: PageIndex SDK Local (8.5/10). Locally executable document retrieval with traceable page citations.
  • Research: Lenz (8/10). Multi-step fact-checking with a source trail for AI-generated claims.
  • Agents: Construct Computer (8/10). Persistent agent workspace with a cloud computer and activity log.

item.title: Week 34/2026: ChatGPT for Teens, ElevenLabs AI Caption Generator, Databricks Genie One, ChatPlayground AI, Berd
item.description:
This week is less about the next model showcase than about controllable work contexts. ChatGPT for Teens shows how text AI can encourage learning paths instead of shortcuts. ElevenLabs reduces subtitling to an editable production step, while Genie One ties answers to governance and company data. ChatPlayground makes contradictions visible, and Berd brings agents back closer to local projects and one's own rules.

  • Text: ChatGPT for Teens (8/10). Learning-oriented text AI with additional safeguards for young people.
  • Design: ElevenLabs AI Caption Generator (9/10). Time-synchronised subtitles as a fast, editable production step.
  • Data / Knowledge: Databricks Genie One (8/10). Governed answers and follow-up actions on company data in natural language.
  • Research: ChatPlayground AI (7/10). Compare several AI models, see contradictions and ask better research questions.
  • Agents: Berd (8/10). Open-source desktop workspace for local projects, skills and specialised agents.

item.title: Week 33/2026: Writer Agent + effizientes Harness, Grok Imagine Image 2.0, Muse Glimmer, Perplexity Computer for Builders, Claude Code Auto Mode
item.description:
This week AI shifts from individual outputs to controllable execution. Writer optimises the cost structure of agentic text work, Claude Code combines autonomy with an additional safety mechanism. For visual teams, precise editing becomes more important than another prompt lottery ticket. Muse Glimmer shows how local open weights put data protection and control back into one's own hands.

  • Text: Writer Agent + effizientes Harness (8/10). Agentic text work focused on cost control, context and governance.
  • Design: Grok Imagine Image 2.0 (8/10). Image generation and precise editing for production-grade creative work.
  • Data / Knowledge: Muse Glimmer (9/10). Open-weights model for local knowledge assistants, tool use and agentic workflows.
  • Research: Perplexity Computer for Builders (8/10). Research and execution workflow across code, product data, payments and telemetry.
  • Agents: Claude Code Auto Mode (9/10). Longer-running coding agents with risk-based safety checks instead of endless clicking.

item.title: Week 30/2026: Substack Pangram AI Detection, FLUX 3 (Black Forest Labs), Gemini 3.6 Flash (Google), Perplexity Computer Brain, HubSpot Agent Hub & Agent Builder
item.description:
Week 30 is about transparency, efficiency and the maturity of AI agents. Substack brings an important tool for content authenticity with Pangram, Black Forest Labs advances multimodal generation with FLUX 3, and Google makes agent workflows much cheaper with Gemini 3.6 Flash. Perplexity addresses the fundamental amnesia problem of current AI tools, while HubSpot Agent Hub shows what agent infrastructure looks like in day-to-day business.

  • Text: Substack Pangram AI Detection (8/10). A tool integrated into Substack for detecting AI-generated text.
  • Design: FLUX 3 (Black Forest Labs) (9/10). FLUX 3 is the new multimodal foundation model from the German start-up Black Forest Labs.
  • Data / Knowledge: Gemini 3.6 Flash (Google) (9/10). Google's new efficiency model with 1M token context, 17% fewer output tokens and a lower price.
  • Research: Perplexity Computer Brain (10/10). Self-improving memory system for the Perplexity Computer agent.
  • Agents: HubSpot Agent Hub & Agent Builder (9/10). Central workspace in HubSpot for AI agents in marketing, sales and service.

item.title: Week 29/2026: Inkling von Thinking Machines, Google Vids, NVIDIA Nemotron 3 Embed, Context.dev, Osaurus
item.description:
This week shows that the value of AI lies less in individual demo features than in control over model, knowledge and execution. Inkling and NVIDIA Nemotron 3 Embed open up central model and retrieval layers, Google Vids integrates video more closely into existing workflows, Context.dev structures web data and Osaurus brings agents locally to the Mac. For decision-makers the order stays sober: clarify the data flow, choose a narrowly scoped pilot, measure quality and cost.

  • Text: Inkling von Thinking Machines (8/10). Open-weights model for multimodal text, image and audio workflows
  • Design: Google Vids (8/10). Workspace video editor with Gemini Omni Flash and personal avatars
  • Data / Knowledge: NVIDIA Nemotron 3 Embed (9/10). Open embedding models for RAG, semantic search and agent memory
  • Research: Context.dev (8/10). Web context API for scraping, crawling and structured extraction
  • Agents: Osaurus (8/10). Native macOS agents with local models and optional cloud providers

item.title: Week 20/2026: Shadow, Aaavatar, Kanwas, AnySearch, Mindra
item.description:
The most interesting development this week is that AI tools connect context and execution. Shadow handles meeting follow-ups during the call, Kanwas organises product knowledge for people and agents, and Mindra builds operational agent teams from it. Aaavatar shows that data protection can be a real advantage in design tools when processing is local-first. AnySearch makes clear that good agents need better access to information, not only better models.

  • Text: Shadow (8/10). Real-time assistant for calls, follow-ups and meeting to-dos
  • Design: Aaavatar (8/10). Local-first Mac app for consistent team portraits
  • Data / Knowledge: Kanwas (8/10). Shared context workspace for product teams and agents
  • Research: AnySearch (7/10). Search API infrastructure for AI agents and vertical data sources
  • Agents: Mindra (8/10). Multi-agent orchestration for operational workflows

item.title: Week 19/2026: Postwise AI, Flowstep 1.0, Exmergo Viz, Web of Science Research Intelligence, Claude Financial Services Agents
item.description:
This week the market visibly shifts from isolated generators to AI systems embedded in real work processes. Postwise and Flowstep show how individuals and small teams publish and visualise faster. Exmergo Viz opens up data analysis but demands clean governance. Web of Science Research Intelligence and Claude Financial Services Agents show the enterprise side: curated data, traceable workflows and controllable agents are becoming standard. The question is no longer whether AI can do something, but whether it may do it responsibly in the right process.

  • Text: Postwise AI (8/10). Social writing and scheduling for X, LinkedIn and Threads
  • Design: Flowstep 1.0 (8/10). AI design engineer for editable UI flows and Figma handover
  • Data / Knowledge: Exmergo Viz (7/10). AI dashboards from CSV, Excel and databases via natural language
  • Research: Web of Science Research Intelligence (8/10). AI-native research intelligence for funding, strategy and impact
  • Agents: Claude Financial Services Agents (9/10). Ten agent templates for pitchbooks, KYC, market analysis and finance operations

item.title: Week 18/2026: Genspark for Word, Bitgrain, TrafficClaw, Claude Creative Connectors, Buda
item.description:
Week 18 shows a clear trend towards deep integration of AI agents into existing workflows. Genspark for Word brings capable AI directly into Microsoft 365, while Buda offers a complete platform for building an AI company. TrafficClaw rethinks web analytics with an AI chat interface, and Bitgrain positions itself as a lightweight, flexible design alternative. Anthropic also greatly extends Claude's creative options with new connectors. Trend of the week: agentic workflows inside standard tools. AI leaves isolated chat interfaces and is embedded directly in Microsoft Office, design software and analytics dashboards.

  • Text: Genspark for Word (9/10). AI agents native to Microsoft 365: drafting, editing and research directly in Word
  • Design: Bitgrain (8/10). Lightweight browser-based design studio focused on textures and dithering
  • Data / Knowledge: TrafficClaw (8/10). Google Analytics alternative with AI chat and a real-time 3D globe
  • Research: Claude Creative Connectors (9/10). Anthropic integrates Claude directly into professional creative software
  • Agents: Buda (9/10). Cloud-native platform for building and managing an AI workforce

item.title: Week 17/2026: Chronicle, ChatGPT Images 2.0, DeepSeek V4, Gemini Deep Research Max, OpenAI Workspace Agents
item.description:
Week 17 marks a concentration of autonomous workflows: OpenAI, Google and DeepSeek simultaneously ship products that move from single prompts to agents that run continuously. ChatGPT Images 2.0 sets a new standard in design with thinking-based image generation. DeepSeek V4 again delivers open-source quality at frontier level for a fraction of the price. Chronicle establishes itself as a serious PowerPoint competitor for teams. The message of the week: AI agents are becoming team infrastructure, no longer just individual tools.

  • Text: Chronicle (8/10). Cursor for slides: enterprise-grade AI presentations with agentic workflows
  • Design: ChatGPT Images 2.0 (9/10). First image generation model with thinking: error-free text, web browsing, precise control
  • Data / Knowledge: DeepSeek V4 (9/10). 1.6T open-source parameters, 1M context as standard, frontier quality at a fraction of the price
  • Research: Gemini Deep Research Max (9/10). MCP support, native charts and Gemini 3.1 Pro: autonomous research at enterprise level
  • Agents: OpenAI Workspace Agents (9/10). Codex agents for teams: always running, Slack-integrated, enterprise controls

item.title: Week 16/2026: Fathom 3.0, Figma for Agents, Google Gemma 4, Perplexity Computer (Personal CFO), Claude Opus 4.7
item.description:
This week was all about agentic workflows and integrating AI into existing systems. Anthropic released Claude Opus 4.7, its strongest model for autonomous tasks, while Figma closes the gap between AI-generated code and design systems with its new MCP server. Perplexity extends its Computer agent into a "personal CFO", and Google brings a very capable local open-source model with Gemma 4. Fathom 3.0 shows how meeting AI can work without intrusive bots.

  • Text: Fathom 3.0 (9/10). Bot-free meeting AI: recording without a visible participant, CRM sync, account-wide insights
  • Design: Figma for Agents (10/10). MCP server connects AI agents with design systems, bidirectional code-canvas workflows
  • Data / Knowledge: Google Gemma 4 (9/10). Multimodal open-source model running locally, 256K context, text, image, audio and video, fully GDPR-compliant
  • Research: Perplexity Computer (Personal CFO) (8/10). AI agent with real-time bank data: spending analysis, budget planning and net-worth tracking via Plaid
  • Agents: Claude Opus 4.7 (10/10). 87.6% on SWE-bench Verified, 1M token context at no extra charge, 3.3x better vision, the new benchmark

item.title: Week 15/2026: UPDF 2.5, Google Veo 3.1 Lite, Gemini Notebooks + NotebookLM, Gemini Interactive Simulations, Claude Managed Agents
item.description:
Week 15/2026 was about productivity gains and agent infrastructure. Google dominated the headlines with three major releases: integrating NotebookLM directly into the Gemini app creates a new model for personal knowledge management, while the new interactive 3D simulations in Gemini change how complex concepts are researched and visualised. Google also cut the cost of AI video generation to just 5 cents per clip with Veo 3.1 Lite. In the enterprise sector, Anthropic set a new standard for deploying AI agents in production with the launch of "Claude Managed Agents" (public beta). UPDF 2.5, presented as the first PDF editor built entirely on autonomous AI agents, rounds off the week.

  • Text: UPDF 2.5 (8.5/10). PDF editor with autonomous AI agents: 10+ specialised agents for research, legal and finance
  • Design: Google Veo 3.1 Lite (9/10). AI video for 0.05 dollars per clip, 50% cheaper than its predecessor, 720p, via the Gemini API
  • Data / Knowledge: Gemini Notebooks + NotebookLM (9.5/10). Personal knowledge base directly in Gemini: persistent projects, source sync, no model training
  • Research: Gemini Interactive Simulations (9/10). 3D models and interactive physics simulations directly in the chat, "show me" instead of static diagrams
  • Agents: Claude Managed Agents (9.5/10). Fully hosted agent infrastructure from Anthropic, public beta, 0.08 dollars per session hour, much faster development

item.title: Week 14/2026: Atomic Chat, Noon, Google Gemma 4, Perplexity Computer for Taxes, Holo3 by H Company
item.description:
Week 14/2026 marks a landmark week for open-source AI: Google released Gemma 4 under the Apache 2.0 licence for the first time, a shift that directly challenges proprietary cloud models. H Company's Holo3 sets a new standard for computer-use agents with 78.85% on the OSWorld benchmark, ahead of GPT-5.4 and Claude Opus 4.6, as a European company under Apache 2.0. In data protection, Atomic Chat stands out: the open-source tool runs completely offline on the Mac, without a single byte leaving the device. The week is rounded off by Noon leaving stealth mode with 44 million dollars for the first AI-native design tool on production code, and by Perplexity Computer's new tax module for US tax returns.

  • Text: Atomic Chat (8.5/10). Open-source ChatGPT alternative: 1,000+ AI models fully offline on the Mac, zero data exfiltration
  • Design: Noon (7.5/10). The first AI-native design tool on production code, 44M dollars in funding, out of stealth mode
  • Data / Knowledge: Google Gemma 4 (9.5/10). Frontier open-source AI under Apache 2.0, from Raspberry Pi to H100, GDPR-compliant on-premise
  • Research: Perplexity Computer for Taxes (7.8/10). First agentic tax assistant: fills in IRS forms, checks returns, optimises deductions
  • Agents: Holo3 by H Company (9.2/10). State-of-the-art computer-use agent, 78.85% on OSWorld, open source Apache 2.0, European company

item.title: Week 13/2026: Pendium, Omma by Spline, Littlebird, Claude Computer Use, Agentplace
item.description:
Week 13 of 2026 shows a strong trend towards autonomous agents and their safe integration into existing workflows. While Anthropic enables AI to control computers directly with "Claude Computer Use", platforms such as Agentplace provide the infrastructure to deploy such agents with clear guardrails. In marketing, tools like Pendium shift the focus from classic SEO to "AI visibility", so that brands appear in the answers of AI models. In design, Omma by Spline sets new standards by using parallel agents to create 3D worlds and interactive websites.

  • Text: Pendium (8.5/10). AI visibility platform: monitor and optimise visibility in ChatGPT, Claude and Gemini
  • Design: Omma by Spline (9/10). Parallel AI agents create 3D websites and apps from text prompts
  • Data / Knowledge: Littlebird (8.8/10). Context-aware Mac AI assistant that continuously understands screen and meetings
  • Research: Claude Computer Use (9.5/10). Anthropic gives Claude direct computer access: AI operates desktop apps autonomously
  • Agents: Agentplace (8.7/10). No-code platform for specialised AI agents in real business workflows

item.title: Week 12/2026: Fathom Commentary Writer, Gamma Imagine, Genie by Databox, Perplexity Comet für iOS, Skyvern
item.description:
Week 12/2026 marks the move from general AI assistants to deeply integrated, context-aware workflow tools. Gamma Imagine shows how a design tool with almost 100 million users redefines the field: no more templates and manual editing, but prompt-to-design in seconds with automatic brand consistency. Skyvern shows that browser automation is finally becoming reliable, thanks to computer vision instead of fragile DOM selectors. Genie by Databox opens up data access for management, Perplexity Comet brings deep research to the iPhone, and Fathom Commentary Writer addresses hallucinations in financial reporting through symbolic attribution.

  • Text: Fathom Commentary Writer (8.5/10). AI financial commentary with symbolic attribution: every number traceable to its source
  • Design: Gamma Imagine (9.5/10). AI-native design canvas for infographics, logos and marketing assets via text input
  • Data / Knowledge: Genie by Databox (8.8/10). AI analyst for business data: natural language queries over your own metrics and KPIs
  • Research: Perplexity Comet für iOS (9.2/10). AI-native browser now on iPhone: deep research, voice mode and agentic browsing
  • Agents: Skyvern (9/10). Open-source browser automation with LLMs and computer vision, self-hostable

item.title: Week 11/2026: Teract, Canva Magic Layers, OrangeLabs, Citable, Naoma AI
item.description:
Week 11/2026 marks the move from general AI assistants to vertical work tools with clear ROI logic. Naoma AI shows how AI agents step directly into the sales process and turn website traffic into personalised product demos. Citable makes a new growth vector visible: the presence of brands in answers from ChatGPT, Perplexity and other AI systems. OrangeLabs opens up access to data, documents and web research through an affordable analysis workspace. Teract professionalises building personal visibility across several networks, and Canva Magic Layers shows how established platforms integrate AI as a natural extension of the existing creative workflow rather than an add-on.

  • Text: Teract (8.3/10). AI reputation coach for LinkedIn, X, Reddit and other platforms
  • Design: Canva Magic Layers (8.4/10). Context-aware AI image editing directly in the Canva workflow
  • Data / Knowledge: OrangeLabs (7.9/10). Talk to your data: documents, CSVs and web search in one analysis workspace
  • Research: Citable (8.1/10). GEO / AI visibility platform for brand presence in AI answers
  • Agents: Naoma AI (8.8/10). AI video sales agent for personalised product demos and lead qualification

item.title: Week 10/2026: GPT-5.4, Variant, Parsewise, Heywa, Luma Agents
item.description:
Week 10/2026 is defined by leaps in performance and new approaches: GPT-5.4 sets new standards for professional workflows with its "thinking" architecture and scores 83% on GDPval, ahead of all predecessors. Variant changes the design process with an endless, scrollable feed of UI designs: no empty canvas, no prompt engineering. Parsewise brings Cursor-like intelligence to documents and addresses the large market of insurance and finance. Heywa replaces the wall of text in ChatGPT with interactive, visual stories, a shift in research UX. Luma Agents shows that a complete advertising campaign worth 15 million dollars can be produced in 40 hours for 20,000 dollars.

  • Text: GPT-5.4 (9/10). OpenAI's new flagship: "thinking" layer, 83% GDPval, 1.05M token context
  • Design: Variant (8.5/10). Endless designs by scrolling: no canvas, no Figma, no prompt engineering needed
  • Data / Knowledge: Parsewise (8.5/10). Cursor for documents: AI agents analyse thousands of PDFs at once with source references
  • Research: Heywa (8/10). Visual stories instead of walls of text: AI research as an interactive mini app
  • Agents: Luma Agents (9/10). A 15M dollar campaign in 40 hours for 20K dollars: creative end-to-end agents with unified intelligence

item.title: Week 09/2026: Mercury 2, QuiverAI (Arrow-1), Supaboard, Perplexity Computer, Notion Custom Agents
item.description:
Week 9/2026 marks a break in AI development: speed, accessibility and orchestration take centre stage. The standout event was the launch of Mercury 2 by Inception Labs, the first diffusion-based reasoning model, which opens up a new speed dimension at more than 1,000 tokens per second. QuiverAI entered the stage with Arrow-1, the first dedicated AI model for vector graphics, which immediately topped the SVG Arena leaderboard and raised 8.3 million dollars from a16z. Perplexity Computer redefines the AI agent by orchestrating 19 different models into one autonomous workflow system. Notion Custom Agents brings 24/7 AI automation into one of the most widely used workspaces, without programming, and Supaboard shows that data analysis no longer requires expert knowledge when you can simply ask in English.

  • Text: Mercury 2 (9/10). Fastest reasoning LLM, diffusion architecture with 1,009 tokens per second and four times lower prices
  • Design: QuiverAI (Arrow-1) (8.5/10). First AI model for vector graphics: editable SVGs from text prompts, number one on SVG Arena
  • Data / Knowledge: Supaboard (8/10). Ask your data in plain English: #1 on Product Hunt in February 2026, 600+ integrations, no SQL needed
  • Research: Perplexity Computer (8.5/10). 19 AI models orchestrated: an autonomous multi-model agent for complex workflows, 200 dollars per month
  • Agents: Notion Custom Agents (8.5/10). 24/7 autonomous AI agents directly in Notion, free until May 2026, no coding required

item.title: Week 08/2026: Claude Sonnet 4.6, Moda, Boost.space v5, Figr AI, Clawi.ai
item.description:
Week 8/2026 followed a clear trend: top performance is becoming more accessible, and tools are becoming more precisely specialised. The biggest event was the release of Claude Sonnet 4.6, which brings Opus-level intelligence at Sonnet prices and resets the price-performance ratio for AI models. Moda addresses one of the biggest frustrations with AI design tools: the lack of editability. Boost.space v5 tackles a fundamental problem for companies working with several AI agents through its "shared context" approach. Figr AI and Clawi.ai complete the week with specialised solutions for UX research and broader access to AI agents.

  • Text: Claude Sonnet 4.6 (9.5/10). Opus-level intelligence at Sonnet prices, Anthropic's new default model
  • Design: Moda (8.5/10). AI design with a fully editable canvas, no restart for every change
  • Data / Knowledge: Boost.space v5 (8/10). Shared context for AI agents: a common brain for all automations
  • Research: Figr AI (8/10). Product-aware AI for UX that analyses real apps and reasons through design decisions
  • Agents: Clawi.ai (8/10). OpenClaw in the cloud: a capable AI agent without server setup, controllable via WhatsApp

item.title: Week 05/2026: OpenAI Prism, AirMusic v1.1, Pandada AI, The Prompting Company, Agentic Vision in Gemini
item.description:
This week focused on fundamental developments and new platforms that aim less at single features than at new ways of working. OpenAI launched Prism, a free AI-assisted platform for scientific writing with the potential to change academic collaboration. Google moved image recognition towards an agentic, interactive process with Agentic Vision in Gemini. In data analysis, Pandada AI stood out on Product Hunt by making unstructured data usable for professional reports.

  • Text: OpenAI Prism (9/10). AI-native workspace for scientific writing with GPT-5.2
  • Design: AirMusic v1.1 (7.5/10). AI music generator with royalty-free licensing
  • Data / Knowledge: Pandada AI (8.5/10). AI-assisted data analysis without programming skills
  • Research: The Prompting Company (8/10). SEO for the AI era: optimising for citations in ChatGPT
  • Agents: Agentic Vision in Gemini (9/10). Major Google update for agent-like visual interaction

item.title: Week 04/2026: ContentPod, HouseGPTs, Pandada AI, NBot AI, Smart Calendars AI v2.5
item.description:
Week 4/2026 brought tools that focus on simplifying complex tasks, from content creation to data analysis. ContentPod rethinks content production with a voice-first approach, while HouseGPTs delivers photorealistic home designs in seconds. Pandada AI opens up data analysis through natural language, NBot AI monitors the web around the clock for free, and Smart Calendars AI v2.5 brings agentic AI into everyday scheduling.

  • Text: ContentPod (8/10). Voice-first content creation platform: speak instead of write
  • Design: HouseGPTs (7/10). AI-powered home design platform, photorealistic interiors in seconds
  • Data / Knowledge: Pandada AI (8/10). Natural language data analysis platform: ask your data in plain language
  • Research: NBot AI (7/10). Personal AI radar for content curation, free 24/7 web monitoring
  • Agents: Smart Calendars AI v2.5 (8/10). Agentic AI calendar assistant: create appointments by speaking, photographing or pasting

item.title: Week 03/2026: TranslateGemma, GLM-Image, NotebookLM Data Tables, Xpoz MCP, Claude Code MCP Tool Search
item.description:
Calendar week 3 of 2026 was shaped by significant releases from the major AI players.
